title: AI Style & Verbosity Controls: Rules That Beat Adjectives
description: Replace vague persona adjectives with 5 deterministic style controls: opening rule, list threshold, hedge cap, pushback trigger, and uncertainty clause.
h1: AI style and verbosity controls: 5 deterministic rules that beat adjectives.
dek: Telling an LLM to 'be concise, smart, and natural' barely moves output structure. Giving it five checkable structural triggers changes every reply.
lede: Most custom instructions fail because they rely on subjective mood words like “Write in a crisp, senior, no-fluff, conversational tone.” Models follow checkable structural rules—like where to put the answer and when to use a list—far more reliably than adjectives.
answer: Replace vague tone adjectives with five checkable rules: (1) Opening Rule ('state the answer in sentence one'), (2) List & Table Threshold ('prose by default; lists or tables only for 3+ items'), (3) Proportional Verbosity ('1–3 sentences for lookups, full tradeoffs for high-stakes decisions'), (4) Pushback Trigger ('name the weakest assumption before implementing'), and (5) Uncertainty Clause ('flag material uncertainty instead of guessing').

sections.html:
Control dimensionWeak adjective (drifts fast)Deterministic rule (persists across long chats)
1. Opening structure"Don't waste my time with fluff.""State the direct answer, fix, or recommendation in sentence one—no restating my question."
2. Formatting density"Write naturally like a human.""Default to plain paragraphs; use bullets for sequential steps and tables only when comparing 3+ items on shared criteria."
3. Length / verbosity"Be super concise.""Scale length to task stakes: 1–3 sentences for factual lookups; structured tradeoffs for architecture, money, or irreversible actions."
4. Epistemic candor"Don't be sycophantic.""Never open with praise. If my plan has a flaw or cleaner alternative, state the objection and evidence before executing."
5. Confidence & gaps"Be accurate and confident.""Separate verified facts from inference, and flag material uncertainty explicitly instead of guessing."

sections.h2: What measured pilot data shows when you use explicit controls.
sections.html:
We tested explicit structural rules against untuned defaults in our 60-reply before/after pilot (20 real tasks × 3 setups):

  • Answer-first rate (5/5 rubric score): Rose from 14/20 on default prompts to 19/20 with explicit rules.
  • Hedging phrases per reply: Dropped from 0.35 to 0.05.
  • Trailing follow-up questions: Dropped from 0.90 to 0.25 when the prompt limited questions to real blockers.

Always pair anti-hedging rules with rule #5 (“flag material uncertainty explicitly”). Banning filler disclaimers (“As an AI...”) should sharpen real technical caveats—never force the model to guess when facts are missing. Our Instruction Checker flags prompts that accidentally ban honest uncertainty.

Profile A: High-density analytical prose (engineers, researchers, analysts)

## Style & register controls - Opening: Lead with the answer, root cause, or recommendation in sentence one. - Format: Default to dense, clear prose; use code blocks for exact commands and tables only when comparing 3+ options. - Verbosity: 1–3 sentences for simple lookups; mechanism-first depth when correctness or architecture is at stake. - Pushback: Challenge weak premises or overengineered plans before implementing them. - Uncertainty: Separate verified facts from inference and flag material uncertainty explicitly.

Profile B: Rapid operator brief (founders, PMs, triage)

## Style & register controls - Opening: State the recommended decision and expected impact in the first two lines. - Format: Maximum 5 bullets for multi-part updates; plain 2-sentence paragraphs otherwise. - Tradeoffs: When options are close, name the single deciding variable rather than listing ten pros and cons. - Questions: Ask at most one clarifying question only if missing context flips the recommendation; otherwise state your assumption and proceed.

Profile C: Exploratory thinking partner (design, writing, strategy)

## Style & register controls - Opening: Address my core question directly without generic praise or throat-clearing. - Exploration: Surface 2–3 genuinely distinct angles (including one non-obvious counter-perspective) before narrowing to a single answer. - Register: Write in clean, concrete prose—avoid corporate buzzwords, clichés, and bulleted walls. - Honesty: Point out blind spots candidly while keeping space open to iterate.

Tune all five controls interactively in our Communication Preferences Builder, or see how to stop AI sycophancy.

faq.q: How do I stop ChatGPT or Claude from putting bullet points in every single answer?
faq.a: Don't write 'Never use bullet points'—write a threshold rule: 'Default to plain paragraphs. Use bullet lists only for sequential steps and tables only when comparing 3 or more items across shared criteria.' Threshold rules stop reflex bullets without breaking checklists.

faq.q: Why does 'be concise' make AI answers unhelpful on hard problems?
faq.a: A flat 'be concise' instruction penalizes depth equally on trivial lookups and complex debugging. Use proportional verbosity instead: '1–3 sentences for simple factual questions; full mechanism and tradeoffs for architecture, security, or irreversible changes.'

faq.q: Do personality labels like 'Act as an INTJ' work better than explicit style rules?
faq.a: Explicit behavioral rules carry the predictable effect because the model can verify 'answer in sentence one' directly. Personality types (MBTI, DISC, Enneagram) are most useful as a fast human discovery shortcut for choosing which explicit rules fit you—see our 180-reply comparison protocol for testing label vs plain-English rules.

faq.q: How do I cut AI hedging without encouraging hallucinated certainty?
faq.a: Ban performative throat-clearing ('Great question!', 'It is important to remember...') while explicitly requiring calibrated uncertainty ('Separate verified facts from inference and state material uncertainty when evidence is incomplete').
